stem: A printing press prints the pages of a large order at a constant rate from start to finish. 24 minutes after the press starts, \(\frac{3}{5}\) of the order remains to be printed. How many minutes after that will \(\frac{1}{6}\) of the order remain to be printed?
solution: In 24 minutes the press printed \(1 - \frac{3}{5} = \frac{2}{5}\) of the order, so the whole order takes \(24 \div \frac{2}{5} = 60\) minutes.
\(\frac{1}{6}\) of the order remains when \(\frac{5}{6}\) is printed, at \(\frac{5}{6} \cdot 60 = 50\) minutes after the start.
That is \(50 - 24 = 26\) minutes after the 24-minute mark.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{1}{6}\) of the 60-minute job, the time needed to print \(\frac{1}{6}\) of the order, not the time until \(\frac{1}{6}\) remains.
explanation.B: Correct. The job takes 60 minutes in total; \(\frac{1}{6}\) remains at 50 minutes, which is 26 minutes after the 24-minute mark.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(60 - 24\), the time until the order is completely printed, not until \(\frac{1}{6}\) of it remains.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the time from the start of the job until \(\frac{1}{6}\) remains; the question asks how many minutes after the 24-minute mark.

verify:
t = symbols('t')
T = solve(Eq(1 - 24/t, Rational(3, 5)), t)[0]
assert T == 60
r = 1 - t/T
t2 = solve(Eq(r, Rational(1, 6)), t)[0]
assert t2 == 50
ans = t2 - 24
assert ans == 26
assert value(choices[answer]) == ans
assert all(value(choices[k]) != ans for k in choices if k != answer)
